input.strategy_title: Bundle an S3-compatible object store for disconnected installs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Pipelines and model serving both require S3-compatible object storage, but
disconnected customers frequently have none. Field teams work around this by
installing upstream MinIO ad hoc — unsupported, unpatched, and invisible to the
platform. We want a supported, bundled S3-compatible store that administrators
can enable for disconnected and PoC clusters. The leading candidate, MinIO, is
AGPL-3.0 licensed; redistribution terms must be cleared before any productization
work can ship, and the outcome may force a different upstream.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Legal review of redistributing the candidate object store (MinIO, AGPL-3.0) is completed and documented, including the derivative-work posture for operator integration. This clearance blocks all shipping work. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Administrators can enable a supported, bundled S3-compatible object store through the Platform Operator, with productized images and upgrade lifecycle. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Data Science Pipelines and model serving connection defaults can target the bundled store without manual endpoint configuration. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers enablement, sizing guidance, and the supported/unsupported boundary versus customer-provided storage. |

## Affected Components

- Platform Operator
- Data Science Pipelines
- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Replacing customer-provided S3 in connected environments
- Data migration tooling between stores

## Open Questions

1. If AGPL terms cannot be satisfied for our distribution model, the fallback
   candidate is an Apache-2.0 alternative (e.g. SeaweedFS) — acceptable, but it
   restarts image productization.

# Midstream repo onboarding for MinIO (outcome: AGPL redistribution cleared)

## Description

Create the midstream repository for MinIO under opendatahub-io so the
platform can carry, patch, and productize it as the bundled S3-compatible
object store. This epic executes when the legal redistribution review clears
MinIO (AGPL-3.0) for the product distribution model.

## Scope

- Midstream fork of the MinIO upstream under opendatahub-io.
- Branching/versioning conventions matching the platform's carried-fork
  practice.
- Basic repository hygiene: CI triggers, contribution/automation permissions
  aligned with other opendatahub-io midstream repos.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The midstream MinIO repository exists under opendatahub-io and tracks the
  selected upstream version.
- Repository automation and permissions match the platform's standard
  midstream conventions.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): productized images for the bundled store (repo foundation for
  the MinIO productization chain).

# Productized MinIO container image with upgrade lifecycle (outcome: AGPL redistribution cleared)

## Description

Produce the productized MinIO container image that the Platform Operator
deploys as the bundled S3-compatible object store: pinned version, platform
productization conventions, and a defined upgrade path. The productization work
(build recipe, base-image and labeling conventions, version pinning) is authored
in and built from the midstream MinIO repository, so it begins after the
midstream repo onboarding creates that repository. Within that constraint, the
work proceeds in parallel with the build-pipeline onboarding — the pipeline
gates first execution of the image build, not the start of this work.

## Scope

- Productized container image build for MinIO from the midstream source
  (pinned upstream version, platform base-image and labeling conventions).
- Upgrade path for the image across platform releases, including a
  re-pinnable version strategy for future upstream updates.
- A published image digest that the Platform Operator integration can pin as
  a configuration reference.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A productized MinIO container image is built from the midstream source with
  the pinned version recorded.
- The Konflux build pipeline is green for the image build.
- The image is published with a stable digest available for the operator's
  wiring (the digest is a configuration reference filled in at execution
  time; it does not create a dependency on this work).
- An upgrade path is defined: moving to a newer upstream MinIO version does
  not require redesigning the productization.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): productized images and upgrade lifecycle for the bundled store
  (MinIO chain).

# Midstream repo onboarding for the Apache-2.0 fallback object store (outcome: AGPL redistribution not cleared)

## Description

Create the midstream repository for the Apache-2.0 fallback S3-compatible
object store (e.g. SeaweedFS) under opendatahub-io. This epic executes only
if the legal redistribution review does not clear MinIO — the fallback
restarts image productization against a new upstream. The specific fallback
upstream should be confirmed as the first step of this epic, since the
strategy names SeaweedFS only as an example candidate.

## Scope

- Confirmation of the Apache-2.0 fallback upstream (SeaweedFS unless the
  legal review outcome indicates otherwise).
- Midstream fork of the selected upstream under opendatahub-io.
- Branching/versioning conventions matching the platform's carried-fork
  practice, and basic repository hygiene (CI triggers, permissions).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The fallback upstream is confirmed and documented as the productization
  target.
- The midstream repository exists under opendatahub-io and tracks the
  selected upstream version.
- Repository automation and permissions match the platform's standard
  midstream conventions.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): productized images for the bundled store (repo foundation for
  the fallback productization chain).

# Legal review: redistributing MinIO (AGPL-3.0) in the product distribution

## Description

Resolve the licensing uncertainty that blocks all shipping work for the bundled
S3-compatible object store. Legal reviews whether MinIO (AGPL-3.0) can be
redistributed as part of the product distribution for disconnected installs,
including the derivative-work posture for integrating it with the platform
operator (bundling, deploying, and managing MinIO from our operator). The
outcome is a documented clearance decision.

## Scope

- Legal analysis of AGPL-3.0 redistribution terms under the product's
  distribution model for disconnected / PoC clusters.
- Explicit determination of the derivative-work posture for operator
  integration: whether deploying and managing MinIO from the platform operator
  creates obligations (source availability, notices, offer requirements) and
  what satisfying them requires.
- Documented decision with the conditions of clearance, or a documented
  finding that redistribution is not acceptable.
- If redistribution is not acceptable: confirmation of the fallback candidate
  (an Apache-2.0 alternative, e.g. SeaweedFS) as the productization target.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The legal review is completed and documented, covering redistribution terms
  and the derivative-work posture for operator integration (HLR-1).
- The decision record states, unambiguously, whether MinIO may be bundled, and
  under what conditions.
- If clearance is denied, the record identifies the fallback upstream and
  notes that image productization restarts against it.
- The outcome is communicated to the platform operator, pipelines, and model
  serving teams so downstream work can proceed.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): Legal review of redistributing the candidate object store
  (MinIO, AGPL-3.0) is completed and documented, including the derivative-work
  posture for operator integration.

# Platform Operator enablement of the bundled S3-compatible object store

## Description

Deliver the operator-side capability that lets administrators enable a
supported, bundled S3-compatible object store on disconnected and PoC clusters,
with productized images and a managed upgrade lifecycle. This replaces the
unsupported field practice of installing upstream MinIO ad hoc with a
platform-visible, supported capability.

## Scope

- Administrator-facing enablement of the bundled S3-compatible object store
  through the Platform Operator (opt-in; not enabled by default).
- Deployment and lifecycle management of the bundled store by the operator,
  consuming the productized store container image.
- Upgrade lifecycle for the bundled store across platform upgrades.
- Wiring that allows other platform components to discover and target the
  bundled store's endpoint without manual configuration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An administrator can enable (and disable) the bundled S3-compatible object
  store through the Platform Operator on a disconnected cluster.
- When enabled, the store runs from the productized image; the pinned image
  digest of the productized store is available at wiring time (configuration
  reference — the operator integration does not block on, and is not blocked
  by, the image productization work; each proceeds in parallel).
- The bundled store is not enabled by default; clusters without it behave
  exactly as before (no regression for customer-provided storage).
- The upgrade lifecycle is exercised: the bundled store survives a platform
  upgrade without data loss or manual reconfiguration.
- The store's S3 endpoint is usable by platform components on the same
  cluster without manual endpoint entry.
- The build pipeline for any repository touched by this epic is green.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Administrators can enable a supported, bundled S3-compatible
  object store through the Platform Operator, with productized images and
  upgrade lifecycle.
